newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower despite export sales total.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower despite export sales total.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower despite a large number in USDA's weekly export sales report, traders said.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat in the week ended January 23 totaled 422,900 tonnes, above expectations for 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Traders said the cash basis levels were starting to weaken at the Gulf and there was profit taking of the bull spreads.
Also pressure on wheat came from indications India is in the market for only 50,000 tonnes of wheat and from a larger amount of wheat offered for export this week by the EU.
The EU offered 249,800 tonnes of rebate wheat at a maximum 14.98 Ecus per tonne.
But traders continued to cite the drop in CBOT soybeans as a key factor in the decline of wheat futures.
"Certainly beans led us down and corn's inability to hold firm after the excellent export numbers hurt us," a trader said.
KCBT wheat closed one to four cents per bushel lower, with March down four at $4.12.
